instructions: Return only the requested structured result. Evaluate the supplied rules for symmetry, neutrality, clarity, and reproducibility without inventing or assuming a rationale for them.

content.text: {"verdict":"UNFAIR","agree_to_use_as_baseline":"NO","symmetry":"FAIL","neutrality":"FAIL","reproducibility":"FAIL","strengths":["The candidates are frozen before comparison, reducing post hoc modification.","The admission gate is facially symmetrical and separates inadmissibility from comparative weakness.","Hard admission constraints, comparative evidence, source weighting, and reporting requirements are substantially distinguished.","The rules preserve UNDERDETERMINED and do not force a winner.","The evidence ledger, dependency clustering, reversal audit, and adverse-evidence requirements are strong safeguards against selective reporting and double-counting.","The rules exclude theological usefulness, popularity, familiarity, and source identity alone as positive linguistic evidence.","The decision threshold prevents accumulations of weak or dependent indicators from manufacturing certainty."],"ambiguities":[{"location":"Rule 1, permitted outcomes","problem":"The rules do not define an outcome for both candidates being inadmissible, nor state whether the surviving candidate is automatically better supported when only its rival is inadmissible.","minimum_clarification":"Add `INADMISSIBLE_BOTH` and state that when exactly one candidate is inadmissible, the report records that result without treating the surviving candidate as comparatively proven beyond admissibility."},{"location":"Rules 5 and 12, evidence classes","problem":"“Direct disambiguating textual evidence,” “direct controlling evidence,” and “independent early Hebrew or Aramaic manuscript evidence” overlap. The rules do not specify which class contains pointed, partially pointed, transliterated, or orthographically disambiguating witnesses. Classification can materially change the result.","minimum_clarification":"Define class 1 as evidence that directly encodes the disputed division or vocalization, identify which witness types qualify, and state that an unpointed witness that preserves only the agreed consonants is neutral for the vocalization unless it contains another disambiguating feature."},{"location":"Rule 5, fixed evidence order","problem":"“Progressively broader biblical usage” is placed above “independent early Hebrew or Aramaic manuscript evidence” without defining when manuscript evidence belongs instead to class 1. This makes the hierarchy difficult to apply consistently.","minimum_clarification":"State that disambiguating manuscript evidence belongs to class 1 and that class 5 contains only noncontrolling manuscript evidence not already classified there."},{"location":"Rule 6, whole-explanation comparison","problem":"“Most high-quality evidence” and “fewest unsupported exceptions” are not tied expressly to the fixed hierarchy and could be read as an unstructured overall tally.","minimum_clarification":"Replace that language with: “Prefer a candidate only under Rule 12, evaluating quality by the classes in Rule 5 and never aggregating lower classes to override a clear higher-class result.”"},{"location":"Rule 10, source-risk rule","problem":"“Institutional commitment,” “position at stake,” and “requires independent corroboration” are not operationally defined. A perceived commitment could become an unreviewable reason to discount a source even without demonstrated textual behavior.","minimum_clarification":"Permit adjustment only upon independently documented, relevant, and testable textual or translational behavior, not merely identity, belief, institutional affiliation, or inferred interest."},{"location":"Rule 11.2, appointed times","problem":"“Established calendar commitment,” “materially determines,” and “governing signs” lack objective classification criteria and corpus boundaries.","minimum_clarification":"Delete this topic-specific trigger and apply the revised general source-risk rule, requiring demonstrated relevant textual behavior."},{"location":"Rule 11.3, expressly sealed passages","problem":"The rule does not define who determines that the disputed words are covered by a sealing statement, what “until an appointed time” means operationally, or what historical evidence should probably exist. This may selectively neutralize negative evidence for a novel candidate.","minimum_clarification":"Delete the trigger and apply Rule 9’s general argument-from-silence test equally: silence has weight only when the evaluator establishes that the evidence would probably exist under the candidate."},{"location":"Rule 13, reproducibility","problem":"The report requirements are strong, but the rules do not require predeclared textual editions, witness sets, corpus boundaries, date and dialect classifications, search terms, databases, exclusions, or treatment of negative searches.","minimum_clarification":"Require these items to be fixed and disclosed before evidence collection for the case."},{"location":"Rule 12, additional-class requirement","problem":"“At least one additional independent class” does not say whether neutral evidence qualifies, whether the class must positively favor the candidate, or how a class containing only one dependent family is treated.","minimum_clarification":"State that the additional class must contain positive, materially distinguishing support from an evidentiary family independent of the evidence establishing the highest-class advantage."}],"unfair_rules":[{"rule_id":"R11.1","problem":"It expressly identifies a religiously defined tradition by its position concerning Jesus and imposes special corroboration when adjudicating a specified theological proposition. This is not source-neutral or fully reversible: an otherwise equivalent tradition on the other side is not expressly subjected to the same trigger. Predeclaration does not cure the asymmetry.","minimum_revision":"Delete Rule 11.1. Evaluate every source under a single general rule based only on independently demonstrated textual, scribal, or translational behavior relevant to the precise class of readings."},{"rule_id":"R11","problem":"The three topic-specific heightened-scrutiny categories depart from the otherwise general and candidate-neutral method. They create special procedural treatment for selected theological and calendrical subjects rather than defining a universally applicable source-risk mechanism.","minimum_revision":"Delete Rule 11 in full. Retain only a revised Rule 10 that applies the same documented-behavior test to every source, topic, and candidate."},{"rule_id":"R10, final paragraph","problem":"A mere “demonstrated position at stake” triggers a corroboration requirement even if no relevant tendency in handling texts has been demonstrated. This allows judgments about beliefs or interests to substitute for evidence of source behavior and can impose asymmetric burdens.","minimum_revision":"Replace the paragraph with: “A source’s commitment or interest does not by itself reduce its weight. Additional corroboration may be required only when independent evidence demonstrates a relevant and testable pattern of textual, scribal, or translational behavior for the precise class of readings; the same criterion applies to every source and candidate.”"}],"missing_rules":["A defined outcome and reporting procedure for both candidates failing the admission gate.","A mandatory case-specific protocol freezing the base edition, witness set, target historical question, corpus boundaries, date and dialect assumptions, search procedure, and exclusions before evidence is gathered.","An explicit rule for assigning potentially overlapping evidence to exactly one hierarchy class while recording, but not double-counting, its other attributes."],"comparison_to_own_proposal":"The proposed rules closely match the frozen proposal on fixed consonants, symmetrical admission, hierarchical comparison, dependent-witness clustering, auditable reporting, reversal testing, and preservation of underdetermination. They differ legitimately in giving the received pointing no rebuttable evidentiary presumption; that difference is not inherently procedurally unfair if consistently applied. The decisive departure is Rules 10–11: the frozen proposal permits source adjustment only for a specified, independently demonstrated textual mechanism and rejects adjustment based merely on religious identity or presumed motive. The author's topic-specific and confessionally framed scrutiny rules do not meet that neutrality standard.","exact_revision_suggestions":["Delete Rule 11 in its entirety.","Replace Rule 10’s final paragraph with: “A source’s commitment, identity, affiliation, or interest does not by itself reduce its evidentiary weight. Weight may be adjusted, or independent corroboration required, only when evidence independent of the disputed reading demonstrates a relevant, testable pattern of textual, scribal, or translational behavior for the precise class of readings. Apply the identical criterion to every source and candidate. Such adjustment supplies no positive evidence for the rival.”","Add `INADMISSIBLE_BOTH` to Rule 1 and add: “If exactly one candidate is inadmissible, report that gate result; the other candidate survives but is not thereby shown to be historically original. If both fail, report `INADMISSIBLE_BOTH`. ”","Add after Rule 5.1: “Direct disambiguating textual evidence means a witness feature that actually encodes or necessarily entails the disputed vocalization or division, including qualifying pointing, partial pointing, transliteration, annotation, or orthographic disambiguation. A witness preserving only the agreed unpointed consonants is neutral unless another feature distinguishes the candidates.”","Revise Rule 5.5 to: “Independent early manuscript evidence not already classified as direct disambiguating evidence under class 1.”","Revise Rule 6’s preference sentence to: “Apply the threshold in Rule 12 using the hierarchy in Rule 5. Do not aggregate lower classes to overturn a clear higher-class result, and do not treat the raw number of data as evidentiary weight.”","Clarify Rule 12.2 by replacing “supported by at least one additional independent class” with “positively and materially corroborated by at least one additional evidence class containing an evidentiary family independent of the family establishing the highest-class advantage.”","Add to Rule 13: “Before collecting case evidence, freeze and disclose the base textual edition, witness set, target historical question, chronological and dialectal boundaries, corpus definitions, search terms, databases or editions searched, exclusions, and treatment of negative searches.”","Add to Rule 13: “Each datum must be assigned to one primary hierarchy class. Other relevant attributes may be recorded, but the datum or its dependent descendants may not be counted again in another class.”"],"reasoning":"Most of the framework is balanced and could allow either candidate to lose. Nevertheless, Rules 10–11 introduce a material fairness defect. Rule 11.1 expressly singles out a religiously identified tradition and a specified theological question for heightened scrutiny, while Rules 11.2–11.3 create additional subject-specific exceptions. These provisions are not converted into neutral rules merely by being predeclared. Rule 10 also permits a source’s perceived commitment or stake, without demonstrated relevant textual conduct, to trigger a corroboration burden. That creates a potentially unbounded and contestable source-weight adjustment. Reproducibility is further impaired by overlapping evidence classes and the absence of mandatory corpus and search specifications. Because textual deletion and amendment are required, the rules cannot be accepted exactly as written.","confidence":"HIGH"}
